newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-DODGERS SUFFER FIRST OPENING DAY SHUTOUT IN 27 YEARS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-DODGERS SUFFER FIRST OPENING DAY SHUTOUT IN 27 YEARS.

text.p: The Los Angeles Dodgers were shut out on Opening Day for the first time in 27 years Tuesday, victims of a masterful performance by Philadelphia Phillies starter Curt Schilling.
Schilling allowed two infield hits while striking out 11 over eight innings in the 3-0 Phillies victory.
The Dodgers had not been shut out in their season opener since Cincinnati's Gary Nolan blanked them 4-0 in 1970.
Kevin Stocker had three hits and an RBI and scored the game's first run to help make Terry Francona's debut as Philadelphia manager a successful one.
"Usually, I'm the slowest starter in the league, but today I got some hits. "It was fun, it was a blast," Stocker said.
Schilling allowed infield singles to Wilton Guerrero in the first and Brett Butler in the third before retiring the next 11 batters.
"I feel if I'm healthy, there isn't anything I can't do," Schilling said. "I felt strong, I could've gone out there in the ninth, but I knew I was high in the pitch count."
Ricky Bottalico retired all three batters he faced in the ninth for the save.

In Houston, Shane Reynolds outdueled Cy Young Award winner John Smoltz for eight innings and Pat Listach's sacrifice fly pushed home the winning run as the Astros edged the National League champion Atlanta Braves 2-1.

Reynolds allowed one run and seven hits with two walks, one intentional, and seven strikeouts. Smoltz went the distance in a losing effort, giving up two runs and eight hits with a walk and six strikeouts.
Larry Dierker, who went from the broadcast booth to the dugout with no previous managerial experience was a winner in his debut as Houston skipper.
Chipper Jones accounted for Atlanta's offence with a solo homer in the third.
In San Diego, Chris Gomez, Rickey Henderson and Quilvio Veras homered consecutively to start an 11-run sixth inning that gave the Padres a 12-5 victory over the New York Mets.
The Padres trailed 4-0 before the outburst, which set a National League record for single-inning output on Opening Day. It was one-run short of Cleveland's major-league record.
It was just the third season-opening win in 13 years for the Padres, who got three hits from Tony Gwynn and three RBI from Steve Finley.
Todd Hundley, who set a record for most home runs by a catcher last season, belted a two-run homer for the Mets.
In Cincinnati, Hal Morris went 3-for-4 with three RBI and Willie Greene hit a two-run homer to highlight a four-run first inning as the Reds rocked the Colorado Rockies 11-4.
Winner John Smiley allowed four runs and six hits in six innings as the Rockies picked up where they left off in 1996 when they were one of the worst road teams in the majors.
Kevin Jarvis struck out five in three scoreless innings to pick up his first major league save.
Two-sport star Deion Sanders, who rejoined the Reds after playing in the NFL for the Dallas Cowboys last season, had two hits, stole two bases and scored twice.
In Montreal, pinch-hitter Sherman Obando walked with the bases loaded in the ninth to force Henry Rodriguez in with the winning run as the Expos edged the St Louis Cardinals 2-1.

Montreal got a run in the third when Shane Andrews scored on a single to by Mark Grudzielanek. St Louis tied the game in the sixth when Delino DeShields led off with a triple and scored on a one-out wild pitch by Jim Bullinger.
Rich Batchelor, who loaded the bases and walked in the winning run, took the loss. Ugueth Urbina worked out of a jam in the ninth to earn the win.

At Florida, Kevin Brown allowed just an infield single over seven innings and Moises Alou homered and drove in two runs as the Marlins gave new manager Jim Leyland a 4-2 victory over the Chicago Cubs.
Brown, who led the majors with a 1.89 ERA last year, gave up only a single to rookie Kevin Orie in the fifth inning. He struck out eight and walked two.
Alou, who signed a five-year, $25 million free agent contract with Florida during the off-season, homered in the second off Cubs starter Terry Mulholland and added a sacrifice fly in a two-run fifth.
In San Francisco, Kevin Elster delivered a two-run double to snap a sixth-inning tie as the Pittsburgh Pirates gave new manager Gene Lamont a 5-2 victory over the Giants.
With the score 2-2, Elster doubled to right-centre, bringing home Al Martin and Mark Johnson, who reached with one-out singles off loser Rich Rodriguez.
Julian Tavarez, making his Giants debut, gave up the game-winning hit to Elster, the first batter he faced.
Matt Ruebel pitched out of a sixth-inning jam and worked a scoreless seventh for the win.
